title: Developer Experience Docs - SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines standards, procedures, and canonical fixes for developer-facing documentation maintained by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures (CI/CD and rollback), and the top support issues with canonical fixes.

Audience:
- SDK authors and maintainers
- Technical writers and documentation engineers
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers
- Support and CS engineers who reference canonical fixes

Scope:
- Confluence pages and the Git-backed docs repository (github.com/redwood-inference/docs) in the eng-developer-experience space
- SDKs (python, node, go), quickstarts, API examples, and docs-site CI/CD procedures

Owner and reviewers:
- Document owner: Aisha Patel
- Primary reviewers: Marco Chen, Lila Thompson, Diego Rivera

Standards and conventions (high level):
- Use clear, task-oriented headings with a short intro paragraph per page.
- Provide worked examples: minimal, recommended, and production-ready variants.
- Include copy/pasteable CLI and code snippets for Python, Node, and raw curl/http.
- Include a "Troubleshooting" section on every guide with 3-5 high-likelihood failure modes.
- Every doc must include: title, one-paragraph summary, prerequisites, fast-start (3-5 steps), detailed steps, cleanup, and related links.

Document lifecycle and publishing procedure:
1. Draft changes in a feature branch in the docs repo.
2. Add reviewers and reference related ADRs or API specs.
3. Run docs preview via CI pipeline "docs-preview".
4. Address review comments and obtain reviewer approval in the PR.
5. Merge to main; CI runs "docs-release" to publish to staging, then production after auto-smoke checks.
6. Post-publish: add page to Confluence index and update quickstarts metadata.

Required metadata for every page:
- title, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated
- reviewers (recommended), labels, related_pages, confidentiality (optional)

SDK Guides (structure and requirements):
Every SDK guide must include these sections in order: Overview and use cases; Prerequisites (SDK version, runtimes, auth); Quickstart (3-5 runnable steps); API reference with concise examples; Error handling and retries with recommended backoff; Migration notes for breaking changes; Tests and examples link; Troubleshooting and FAQ.

Minimal Python SDK quickstart (copy/paste):
1) Install:
pip install redwood-sdk

2) Example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(prompt="Write a short summary of Redwood Inference.")
print(resp.text)

Node quickstart (npm):
npm install @redwood/sdk

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: 'Explain Redwood Inference in one paragraph' })
console.log(resp.text)

SDK release and versioning policy:
- Follow semver: major.minor.patch.
- Breaking changes require: ADR, migration guide, and a 2-week beta release.
- Patch/minor releases: changelog entry automatically generated from PR titles.
- Security patches: follow CVE policy; emergency releases use the "docs-exec" runbook.

Quickstarts and templates (catalog and usage):
Canonical quickstarts must live in templates/quickstarts in the docs repo and include: README.md with purpose and runtime matrix; one small runnable app (10-200 LOC) runnable in <10 minutes; CI tests (unit + smoke).

Recommended quickstarts:
- hello-world-text-generation
- chat-widget-embeddings-search
- batch-embeddings-pipeline
- reranking-and-filtering

How to use a template:
1. Clone the repo and run: make setup or ./setup.sh
2. Populate API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
3. Run example: make run or node app.js / python main.py
4. Run tests: make test

API examples (conventions and canonical snippets):
Conventions:
- Use short, focused examples (<30 lines) for text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking.
- Show both SDK and raw HTTP (curl) examples.
- Always include error handling and HTTP status code notes for curl examples.

Canonical curl example (text generation):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'

Canonical Python (requests) example:
import os, requests
resp = requests.post(
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
  headers={
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY")}',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  json={ 'model': 'redwood-1.0', 'input': 'Summarize: Redwood Inference platform' }
)
print(resp.json())

Docs site operating procedures (CI/CD, preview, release, rollback):
Key services and tools:
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs
- preview pipeline: "docs-preview"
- release pipeline: "docs-release"
- CLI helper: rwctl (docs site helpers)
- artifact storage: s3://redwood-docs-builds
- monitors: PagerDuty service "DOCS-SITE-PAGE-FAILURE"

Daily checklist:
- Verify last 24h build success rate > 98%.
- Confirm link-checker report shows 0 critical broken links.
- Review outstanding docs PRs older than 7 days.

Procedure: push a docs change to production:
1. Create PR targeted at main and include a preview link.
2. Wait for automated tests: lint, link-check, accessibility, preview build.
3. Get approval from at least one reviewer listed in the page metadata.
4. Merge; CI will publish to staging. Staging auto-smoke runs.
5. If staging is green, production deployment occurs in the next release window or manually via rwctl deploy --prod.

Rollback procedure:
1. Identify failing release and artifact id.
2. rwctl rollback --artifact <artifact-id> --reason "<brief description>"
3. The system publishes the previous artifact to production and opens a rollback incident channel.
4. Post-mortem: update the page with regression notes and add a test to prevent the regression.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Docs site availability (HTTP 200) SLO: 99.9% monthly
- Build success rate SLO: 99% per week
- Link-checker false-positive acceptance threshold: < 2%
- Publishing SLA for critical security fixes: 4 hours

Top support issues and canonical fixes (DevEx & Support):
1) Issue: "Quickstart fails on first run - missing API key / auth error"
Symptoms: 401 responses; missing REDWOOD_API_KEY in env.
Canonical fix: confirm environment variable is set (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...), for Docker ensure secret passed (docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=...), add README note describing how to obtain API key and required IAM role.

2) Issue: "Docs preview shows build failure (link-check or lint)"
Symptoms: CI logs show link-check or HTML validation failures.
Canonical fix: open preview build log; run local link-check (make link-check); if external link is flaky add to link-check allowlist (.linkcheckrc) with expiry and create follow-up ticket.

3) Issue: "SDK example throws serialization/JSON error"
Symptoms: 400 Bad Request "Invalid JSON body".
Canonical fix: verify Content-Type header present for raw HTTP examples; for SDKs ensure serialize helper is used per SDK guide.

4) Issue: "Streaming responses unexpectedly truncated"
Symptoms: partial text returned; client stops reading stream early.
Canonical fix: confirm SDK runtime supports streaming and example uses streaming API (client.stream_generate(...)); increase client socket/read timeout if large responses expected.

5) Issue: "Examples out-of-date after SDK minor release"
Symptoms: deprecation warnings or missing methods.
Canonical fix: update example snippets to new API surface and add migration notes; pin example to a specific SDK version if needed and open docs PR.

6) Issue: "Quickstart fails in Private deployment (VPC) due to egress restriction"
Symptoms: unable to reach model-store.redwood.ai or auth endpoint.
Canonical fix: for Private deployments replace public hostnames with customer-configured proxy hostnames per Private deployment quickstart; add firewall/NAT egress for quickstart runner and reference eng-private-deployments onprem-packaging.

7) Issue: "Embed/semantic search example returns poor results"
Symptoms: low recall; inconsistent embeddings.
Canonical fix: confirm embedding model matches production, normalize text pre-processing steps (lowercase, strip punctuation) and add to quickstart checklist.

8) Issue: "Docs site build times increased dramatically"
Symptoms: CI build time regression.
Canonical fix: inspect build logs for heavy dependency installs and enable caching for node_modules/pip wheels; split doc builds into incremental builds and add changed-files detection to pipeline.

Canonical triage checklist (for support/CS engineers):
- Step 1: Reproduce locally with same SDK version and environment.
- Step 2: Check SDK changelog for known breaking changes.
- Step 3: Run docs preview to confirm example reproducibility.
- Step 4: If reproducible, create a docs PR with the failing example and link to the support ticket.

Templates and checklist for adding a new quickstart:
- Create README with purpose, prerequisites, and runtime matrix.
- Include LICENSE and SECURITY.md if third-party code is included.
- Add CI tests and a Makefile with: setup, run, test, cleanup.
- Add the page to the Confluence quickstarts index and tag labels: quickstart, template, runtime:<language>.

Contacts:
- Primary: Aisha Patel (DevEx docs owner) - aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- On-call: DevEx PagerDuty (DOCS-SITE-PAGE-FAILURE)

Change log:
- 2025-09-15: Initial draft
